findings.text: §11's second case requires "a record whose `review` role is set only on its node and whose root role is absent" to make `recovery._is_review_run` return true and `_task_identity` return a `"review"` key, but it never pins the record's node id; both predicates also recognise a review by the record's minted node id (`_is_review_node`, `recovery_review_subject.py:25-36`, which both copies call), so a record whose node id carries `review-of-`/`plan-review-of-` already satisfies both assertions before the fix — the very fixture the file already uses (`tests/test_plan_review_prefix_is_one_constant.py:23` builds `PLAN_REVIEW_NODE_PREFIX + "fixture"`). A probe confirms `plan-review-of-abc` yields dispatch True / recovery True, while only a non-minted id (`n-plain-node`) yields dispatch False / recovery True.
